```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
options(width = 72)
has_bidser <- requireNamespace("bidser", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("bidser") >= "0.5.0"
has_fmristore <- requireNamespace("fmristore", quietly = TRUE) &&
  "write_frame_h5" %in% getNamespaceExports("fmristore")
note <- function(pkg) {
  cat(
    '<p class="chunk-note">The chunks in this section need the <code>', pkg,
    "</code> package, which is not installed, so they were not run.</p>",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

This vignette follows a frame through its life outside one R session: imported
from fMRIPrep output, saved to disk, and reopened. Along the way it answers a
question that saving raises: when are two frames, spaces, or arrays *the
same*? It assumes the basics from `vignette("fmridataset")`.

```{r}
library(fmridataset)
```

## Import from fMRIPrep

`read_bids_bold()` opens one subject's preprocessed BOLD runs from an fMRIPrep
derivative tree as a single frame. It uses the `bidser` package to find the
files, reads the BOLD headers and run masks, and settles on one volume space.
It does not read BOLD values.

```{r bids-call, eval = FALSE}
bold <- read_bids_bold(
  "/data/my-study",
  subject = "01",
  task = "memory",
  space = "MNI152NLin2009cAsym"
)
```

The package ships a tiny fMRIPrep tree, with one subject, two runs of three
volumes on a 2 by 2 by 2 grid, and one events file per run, so the rest of
this section runs anywhere `bidser` is installed.

```{r bids-note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !has_bidser}
note("bidser (>= 0.5.0)")
```

```{r bids-read, eval = has_bidser}
untar(
  system.file("extdata", "fmriprep-toy.tar.gz", package = "fmridataset"),
  exdir = tempdir()
)
root <- file.path(tempdir(), "fmriprep-toy")

bold <- read_bids_bold(root, subject = "01", task = "memory")
bold
```

The two runs have different brain masks. By default the frame keeps the
voxels inside both, here three. Nothing is resampled or aligned implicitly:
if the runs were in different spaces, or the choice of mask or echo were
ambiguous, the import would stop and ask you to choose.

```{r bids-space, eval = has_bidser}
feature_ids(bold)
```

Because each subject's masks differ, two subjects imported this way have
different feature spaces, and `bind_observations()` will not stack them. To
put several subjects in one space, give every import the same mask: a group
mask file (`mask = "group_mask.nii.gz"`), or the space of a first import.

```{r bids-shared-mask, eval = has_bidser}
again <- read_bids_bold(
  root,
  subject = "01", task = "memory",
  mask = space(bold)
)
same_space(space(again), space(bold))
```

Data that stay in each subject's native space go in a collection instead
(`vignette("studies")`).

The observation table records each volume's run, its position in the run, its
onset within the run, and the TR, so the run structure is ready to use.

```{r bids-observations, eval = has_bidser}
observations(bold)[, c("run_id", "volume_index", "run_time", "TR")]
temporal_schema(bold)
```

Each run is identified by the acquisition it records (`scan_id`): the BIDS
entities that tell acquisitions apart, such as subject, session, task, and
run, rather than its BIDS run label alone, which is unique only within a
session. The output space, the `desc` label, and the folder are left out, so
the same acquisition has the same IDs whichever space fMRIPrep resampled it
into; the file itself is recorded in the run table's `relative_path`. Each
volume's ID adds its position in the run, counted from one like
`volume_index`.

```{r bids-ids, eval = has_bidser}
observation_ids(bold)[1:2]
```

Reading is lazy. Selecting a run reads only that run's volumes.

```{r bids-read-values, eval = has_bidser}
run_2 <- filter_observations(bold, run_id == "run-2")
collect_assay(run_2)
```

The matching `events.tsv` files are attached as an event table.

```{r bids-events, eval = has_bidser}
events <- table_data(frame_table(bold, "events"))
events[, c("onset", "duration", "trial_type")]
```

```{r bids-cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = has_bidser}
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Save and reopen

`write_frame()` saves a frame to an HDF5 file and `open_frame()` reopens it.
The file format belongs to the `fmristore` package, which writes the file
atomically: a failed write leaves no partial file behind. Reopened assays are
read lazily from the file; opening reads the frame's description, not its
values. `fmristore` is not on CRAN; install it from
<https://bbuchsbaum.r-universe.dev>.

The examples in this section and the next use a small frame with two runs.

```{r frame}
set.seed(3)
voxels <- volume_space(dim = c(3, 3, 2), template = "toy")
values <- matrix(
  round(rnorm(6 * n_features(voxels)), 2),
  nrow = 6, ncol = n_features(voxels)
)
observations <- data.frame(
  .obs_id = sprintf("vol-%02d", 1:6),
  run_id = rep(c("run-1", "run-2"), each = 3),
  TR = 2
)
frame <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = values),
  observations = observations,
  space = voxels,
  metadata = list(study = "toy")
)
```

```{r write-note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !has_fmristore}
note("fmristore")
```

```{r write, eval = has_fmristore}
path <- write_frame(frame, file.path(tempdir(), "toy-frame.h5"))
reopened <- open_frame(path)
reopened
```

The reopened frame has the same IDs, space, run structure, and values.

```{r round-trip, eval = has_fmristore}
identical(observation_ids(reopened), observation_ids(frame))
same_space(space(reopened), space(frame))
temporal_schema(reopened)$run_lengths
identical(collect_assay(reopened), collect_assay(frame))
```

Views over the reopened frame read only what they select.

```{r round-trip-view, eval = has_fmristore}
collect_assay(reopened[c("vol-06", "vol-01"), c("voxel-2", "voxel-1")])
```

A whole study (`vignette("studies")`) is saved with `write_study()` and
reopened with `open_study()`. Here the study holds one frame from one subject,
with a run table describing its runs.

```{r save-study, eval = has_fmristore}
subjects <- entity_frame(
  data.frame(subject_id = "sub-01", age = 34),
  key = "subject_id", entity_type = "subject"
)
run_info <- entity_frame(
  data.frame(run_id = c("run-1", "run-2"), condition = c("rest", "task")),
  key = "run_id", entity_type = "run"
)
described <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = values),
  observations = transform(observations, subject_id = "sub-01"),
  space = voxels,
  entities = list(subject = subjects, run = run_info),
  relations = list(
    volume_subject = key_relation("subject_id", target = "subject"),
    volume_run = key_relation("run_id", target = "run")
  )
)
study <- fmri_study(
  list(main = described),
  entities = list(subject = subjects, run = run_info)
)

study_dir <- write_study(study, file.path(tempdir(), "toy-study"))
reopened <- open_study(study_dir)
reopened
entity(reopened, "run")
```

The saved study is a BIDS derivative dataset, so BIDS tools recognise it. BIDS
supplies the dataset description and the participants table; the package adds
only what BIDS has no place for, its study description (`study.json`, in a
lossless JSON encoding), the storage index (`storage.json`), and one HDF5 file
per frame, and lists them in `.bidsignore`.

```{r study-files, eval = has_fmristore}
list.files(study_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
cat(readLines(file.path(study_dir, "participants.tsv")), sep = "\n")
```

`open_study()` checks every frame against the digest recorded when the study
was written, so a frame file that was replaced or rewritten since is reported
rather than silently used.

```{r write-cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = has_fmristore}
unlink(c(path, study_dir), recursive = TRUE)
```

## What gets saved

A saved frame is a *manifest* plus arrays. The manifest, in the package's FDS
format (version 1), describes everything the frame means: its axis IDs and
tables, its feature space, its assays' names, shapes, and types, its entities,
relations, tables, metadata, and provenance. It says nothing about where the
values are stored. `fds_frame_manifest()` builds it without reading any
values.

```{r manifest}
manifest <- fds_frame_manifest(frame)
names(manifest)
str(manifest$assays$bold[c("name", "dtype", "shape")])
```

The digest of the manifest is the frame's *semantic identity*. Because
storage is not part of the manifest, the same frame has the same digest
however its values are stored, chunked, or moved.

```{r manifest-digest}
semantic <- fds_frame_manifest_digest(frame)

rechunked <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = memory_source(values, chunks = c(2L, 9L))),
  observations = observations,
  space = voxels,
  metadata = list(study = "toy")
)
identical(fds_frame_manifest_digest(rechunked), semantic)
```

The values are not part of the meaning either, so changing them leaves the
digest alone. Renaming one observation changes it.

```{r manifest-digest-values}
doubled <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = values * 2),
  observations = observations,
  space = voxels,
  metadata = list(study = "toy")
)
identical(fds_frame_manifest_digest(doubled), semantic)

renamed <- fmri_frame(
  assays = list(bold = values),
  observations = transform(
    observations,
    .obs_id = replace(.obs_id, 1, "first")
  ),
  space = voxels,
  metadata = list(study = "toy")
)
identical(fds_frame_manifest_digest(renamed), semantic)
```

A frame with ephemeral IDs has no manifest, so random IDs can never reach
disk. Importers that need IDs but have only keys, such as subject, run, and
volume number, can derive them with the `deterministic` policy: each ID is a
hash of a namespace and the row's key values, so the same keys always give
the same ID.

```{r deterministic}
scans <- axis_frame(
  data.frame(subject = "01", run = rep(1:2, each = 3), volume = rep(1:3, 2)),
  axis = "observation",
  id_policy = "deterministic",
  id_namespace = "my-study",
  id_keys = c("subject", "run", "volume")
)
axis_ids(scans)[1:2]
```

## Which identity answers which question

A frame has several identities, each answering a different question. They are
computed separately and never stand in for one another.

| Identity | Answers | Function | Use it to |
|:---------|:--------|:---------|:----------|
| Semantic | Is this the same frame, however stored? | `fds_frame_manifest_digest()` | check that two frames mean the same thing |
| Schema | Could these frames be bound or collected? | `frame_schema_digest()` | check compatibility before combining frames |
| Space | Is this exactly the same feature space? | `same_space()`, `space_digest()` | check that columns line up |
| Source | Is this the same stored array, unchanged? | `source_fingerprint()` | key caches and plans |
| Content | Do these arrays hold the same values? | `content_hash()` | verify numbers; it reads every value |

`identity_descriptor()` returns any of these digests together with its type,
so a digest from one row can never be mistaken for another.

```{r identity}
identity_descriptor(frame)
```

### Fingerprints are not content hashes

A source's *fingerprint* is cheap. It is computed once, when the source is
created, from its description and from evidence that needs no reading, such
as a file's size and modification time. File-backed sources re-check that
evidence before every read and raise an error of class
`fmridataset_error_source_stale` when the file has changed.

An in-memory matrix has no file to observe, so its fingerprint includes a
token unique to the object. Two sources built from the same matrix are two
objects with two fingerprints.

```{r fingerprint}
a <- memory_source(values)
b <- memory_source(values)
identical(source_fingerprint(a), source_fingerprint(b))
```

`content_hash()` identifies an array by its values. It reads the whole array
in bounded blocks, so its cost grows with the number of values, and nothing in
the package calls it for you. It gives the same answer across copies, storage
types, chunk grids, and arrays split into pieces.

```{r content-hash}
identical(content_hash(a), content_hash(b))

as_float32 <- memory_source(values, dtype = "float32", chunks = c(1L, 18L))
identical(content_hash(a), content_hash(as_float32))

stacked <- row_sharded_source(list(
  memory_source(values[1:2, ]),
  memory_source(values[3:6, ])
))
identical(content_hash(a), content_hash(stacked))
```

A fingerprint says *same description, same revision*. A content hash says
*same numbers*. Neither implies the other. To make two in-memory sources
built from the same values share a fingerprint, either let the package hash
them once at creation with `identity = "content"`, or state that they are the
same revision yourself with `revision =`, which hashes nothing.

```{r fingerprint-opt-in}
identical(
  source_fingerprint(memory_source(values, identity = "content")),
  source_fingerprint(memory_source(values, identity = "content"))
)
identical(
  source_fingerprint(memory_source(values, revision = "v1")),
  source_fingerprint(memory_source(values, revision = "v1"))
)
```

The design behind these rules is recorded in the package's
[identity](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmridataset/blob/main/inst/architecture/ADR-006-identity-and-canonicalization.md)
and
[fingerprint](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmridataset/blob/main/inst/architecture/ADR-009-source-fingerprints-and-content-hashes.md)
decision records. To hold several subjects or several frames together, see
`vignette("studies")`.
